The reply changed: the line is the aqee definition's line for a person whose redefined person.edu_kid is true (edu, edu_1098t, edu_ein, tin and the lines 23 to 26 answers). Fix round 3 re-check: both sides read person.tin, whose wording changed identically for both (BUG-0256); a pending renewal still reaches the project's gate through person.itin_applied and not the reply's. The arithmetic is the project's aqee definition.

Fix round 3 re-check: both sides read person.tin, whose wording changed identically for both (BUG-0256); a pending renewal still reaches the project's gate through person.itin_applied and not the reply's. The arithmetic is the project's aqee definition.

The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)"; i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." Same expression as Stage 21; the fixes changed only question wording (person.tin, person.edu_1098t, person.edu_inst, person.x_other) and no project expression. It copies the aqee definition's line for every person, with no eligibility gate (person.edu, person.edu_1098t, the lines 23 to 26 answers, the institution EIN), no student-TIN test and no f8863.paid screen, so a person who is not a student, or whose student fails the tests, gets the amounts; it no longer declares the edu_over refusal (the Stage 21 reply did), so an academic period whose assistance exceeds its expenses is computed rather than refused. The reworded person.tin and person.edu_1098t questions do not reach it, since it reads neither. The arithmetic is the project's aqee definition.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same Schedule SE line 13 (Step 2 copies it); sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi EIC Worksheet B, Part 1 and Part 2 (Schedule SE line 3 less line 13 if you file Schedule SE, otherwise Schedule C line 31), with i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The candidate always takes line 3 less line 13; below the $400 threshold line 13 is zero and line 3 is the Schedule C total, so the value equals the project's choice. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

Form 8606 (2025), Part I: with no 2025 distribution, "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14". With a distribution and basis or nondeductible contributions the reply reads the person's own Form 8606 line 14, as the project does for everyone (and the project refuses the distribution case at its cited f8606.dist and person.ira_dist_gate screens); otherwise basis plus nondeductible contributions, which is line 3 (lines 1 plus 2), the project's amount where Form 8606 is filed; it asks the basis of a person who files no Form 8606 (placement). Its nondeductible amount is ruled at person.ira_nondeductible.

Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (person.hundred: "model changed a published result type"; person.sep_s5_raw and person.sep_s6: "part 'person.sep_rate' is not money", "whole operand is not money"; the f8889 refusal declarations of person.hsa_step1, hsa_share, hsa_deduction, hsa_taxable and hsa_addtax: "collection reference requires sum_over", "comparison operands have incompatible types"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside those errors' dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. Form 8606 (2025), Part I: with no 2025 distribution, "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14". The reply reads the return-level ira.line12a / ira.line12b by role, which sum person.ira_deduction, itself defined from them (ruled at person.ira_deduction), so the line is circular. This line builds on that circular line 12 (ira.line12a / 12b by role).

Ruling: scope; f8606 (2025) Part I: "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14. Do not complete the rest of Part I" when there is no distribution. The candidate takes line 3 without a distribution and the f8606.line14 total otherwise, the project the f8606.line14 total (line 3, refused on a distribution); same value. Triage cannot evaluate it: the 4,555 candidate-unknown records are the cycle inherited from person.ira_deduction. The 11 or 12 project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (stage16.refuse.ira.both_kinds, stage16.refuse.ira.kbh_short, stage16.refuse.person.ira_over_limit, stage16.refuse.ira.over_comp). By reading the structure is now the source's (i1040gi p. 97: "Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 9", "Enter the total of the amounts from Schedule 1, lines 11 through 19a, plus 23 and 25", "Subtract line 4 from line 3", "Subtract line 5 from line 2 in each column"), fixing fix round 2's use of adjusted gross income; it inherits person.ira_cov's dropped self-employed coverage. Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin wording), which this line does not read.

Ruling: model error; adjudicates the declaration, not the tax reading. Not executable: the reply fails validation (person.h_se_line4a_mult: "declared NonNegDollars but the expression does not prove non-negativity"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line's candidate reaches person.h_se_line4a_mult (92.35% of its Schedule SE line 3, which is Schedule C line 31 and can be a loss; its guard uses the product only when line 3 is above zero, but the declared type is not proved) through Schedule 1 lines 15 and 16 in its line 4 (s1.line15 and s1.line16 sum its person.se_line13 and person.s16), so no value of it was computed. By reading: i1040gi p. 97, line 4: "Enter the total of the amounts from Schedule 1, lines 11 through 19a, plus 23 and 25"; line 5: "Subtract line 4 from line 3". The reply recomputes lines 3 to 5 per person from f1040.line9 less Schedule 1 lines 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19a, 24a and 25: it subtracts line 24a (jury duty pay), which line 4 does not list, and omits 23 (lines 12, 14 and 23 are screened by scope.schedule1 ("an adjustment on Schedule 1 line 12, 14 or 23"), so they are zero), so with jury duty pay its modified AGI is too low and line 6 too high.

The reply changed: its line 2 less its worksheet line 5. Its worksheet line 5 (h_ira_line5) copies f1040.line11a, adjusted gross income, which includes the IRA deduction itself, where the source starts from line 9 less the Schedule 1 adjustments other than the IRA deduction (i1040gi p. 97: "Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 9" and "Enter the total of the amounts from Schedule 1, lines 11 through 19a, plus 23 and 25"): a cycle ("cycle at person.ira_line6" in the scratch evaluation), on 363 of its 1,426 completed candidate-unknown records; the others ask ira_work_plan where the interview does not (514) or inherit the section 179 cycle. Fix round 4 re-check: the only project change since fix round 3 is BUG-0259 (person.itin_applied now counts an application to renew an expired ITIN), which this line does not read.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; adjudicates the declaration, not the tax reading. Not executable: the reply fails validation (person.h_se_line4a_mult: "declared NonNegDollars but the expression does not prove non-negativity"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line's candidate reaches person.h_se_line4a_mult (92.35% of its Schedule SE line 3, which is Schedule C line 31 and can be a loss; its guard uses the product only when line 3 is above zero, but the declared type is not proved) through person.ira_line6, so no value of it was computed. By reading, two errors against i1040gi pp. 97-98: (1) line 6: "Is the amount on line 5 less than the amount on line 2? No. STOP None of your IRA contributions are deductible"; the reply's line 6 is zero then and its tiers enter the $200 minimum ("If the result is $200 or more, enter the result. But if it is less than $200, enter $200" applies only to a person who reached line 7); (2) for a joint return where one spouse is covered, the column of the person not covered goes through lines 2 to 7 with $246,000, the $10,000 threshold and 70% ("in the column for the IRA of the person who wasn't covered by a retirement plan, multiply by 70% (0.70)"); the reply enters the full limit for every person not covered, so that spouse keeps $7,000 inside the $236,000 to $246,000 phase-out.

"None of your IRA contributions are deductible" and "If married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse, and the result is $20,000 or more ($10,000 or more in the column for the IRA of a person who wasn't covered by a retirement plan), enter the applicable amount below on line 7"; p. 98, line 7: "But if you checked "No" on either line 1a or 1b, then in the column for the IRA of the person who wasn't covered by a retirement plan, multiply by 70% (0.70)". The reply takes the larger of $200 and either the percentage of line 6 (covered) or the full limit (not covered): it enters $200 where line 6 is zero instead of none, never enters the full limit when line 6 reaches the $10,000 or $20,000 threshold, gives an uncovered person on a joint return with a covered spouse the full limit instead of 70% of line 6, and tests the person's own coverage instead of "no one covered" (line 1a and 1b both No).

The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation on three declarations (person.positive_profits: "declared NonNegDollars but the expression does not prove non-negativity"; person.h_llc31: "'aqee' has no line 'line31'"; person.h_ira_line4: "reference 's1.line23' does not resolve"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside those errors' dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. f1040s2 p. 1, Part II, line 8, "Additional tax on IRAs or other tax-favored accounts. Attach Form 5329 if required"; f5329 p. 2, Part VII, line 49: "Additional tax. Enter 6% (0.06) of the smaller of line 48 or the value of your HSAs on December 31, 2025". New to the open list: the project's line is this person's Form 5329 line 4 plus line 49; the reply's is the Part I tax only (10% of line 3 less the SIMPLE part, plus 25% of the SIMPLE part), so the 6% HSA excess-contribution tax is lost (scratch evaluation: classm.f8880.3 $35.52 against $0.00, completed). It also inherits person.x_l2_all's unneeded answers and declares the x_other refusal (placement). Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin wording), which this line does not read.

Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation on three declarations (person.positive_profits: "declared NonNegDollars but the expression does not prove non-negativity"; person.h_llc31: "'aqee' has no line 'line31'"; person.h_ira_line4: "reference 's1.line23' does not resolve"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside those errors' dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. p590b p. 28, Emergency personal expense distributions: "You are limited to taking one emergency personal expense distribution per calendar year". The reply changed: true when both an exception 22 (domestic abuse) and an exception 23 (emergency) amount are above zero, not when there are two exception 23 distributions; it refuses a return with one of each, which the source allows (scratch evaluation: stage21.blind.e5, completed, False against True), and misses two emergency distributions (stage21.refuse.two23, refused: project True, candidate False). Fix round 3 re-check: the only project change since fix round 2 is BUG-0256 (person.tin wording), which this line does not read.

Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation on five expressions (person.se_line6, person.se_line12 and person.h_se_line4a: "data/alternatives/0/guard must be object"; person.h_sep_10000: "data/count must be string"; person.h_educator_cap: "data/of/1 must be string", project schema), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside those errors' dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. p590b p. 28, Distribution limits: "You are limited to taking one emergency personal expense distribution per calendar year". The line is the refusal gate for exception 23 claimed on more than one Form 1099-R (person.x_n23 above 1). The reply tests whether any exception 22 or 23 amount is above zero, so as the gate it is it would refuse every return claiming exception 22 or 23 once. By reading: stage21.mut.e23_over_cap (one exception 23 distribution, line 4 $200.00): project False, candidate True.

Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation on three expressions (person.positive_profits, person.dc_earned and person.dc_earned_b: "model changed a published result type"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside those errors' dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. p590b p. 28, Emergency personal expense distributions, Distribution limits: "You are limited to taking one emergency personal expense distribution per calendar year". The reply changed: x_l1 not equal to x_l1, always false (its note: no separate emergency distributions), although retirement.is_e23 and retirement.l2_e23 are published; the project's refusal of two exception 23 distributions (stage21.refuse.two23) would never fire.
